claim: Over the closed window 2026-06-18T17:46:37Z to 2026-06-29T01:01:04Z, SOLVENT's wallet on BSC received exactly two external deposits totalling 1203.323289 US dollars of Binance-Peg BSC-USD and had nothing transferred out of it, and once those deposits are subtracted the account is down: its dollar-pegged balance rose by 1179.138701 US dollars against 1203.323289 paid in, so the deposit-adjusted result is a LOSS of 24.184588 US dollars, negative under both denominators published here. That loss is the wallet's and it is not provably the agent's - the wallet sent 113 transactions over the window while the receipt chain names 37 distinct transaction hashes, so most of what the key signed is outside the published record, and chain data cannot separate a trade the agent's engine signed from one an operator signed with the same key. It also excludes gas, paid in a native coin the agent's own equity function never counts, so the true economic loss is larger by an amount neither this record nor that chain can state. And no time-weighted return is published as a figure, because the second deposit lands while most of the account's value sits in a token this record did not price.
falsifier:
Four results refute the claim, one per limb, and any of them refutes it on its own.

(1) If the evidence does not recompute - if either deposit transaction fails any of the twelve properties the registered external-deposit rule implies, or if either window block's timestamp is not the whole second the receipt chain's own first or last receipt records, or if the wallet returns anything but 0x from eth_getCode - the evidence limb is refuted, and the report names every failing property on every failing deposit rather than reporting a share.

(2) If the deposit-adjusted result is not a loss - if closing dollar-pegged balance minus opening dollar-pegged balance minus the external deposits is greater than or equal to zero - the loss limb is refuted, and the gain is published in its place under the same numerator, the same two denominators and the same method. This is the limb a third deposit or any withdrawal would move, and the deposit set is owner-attested from a log sweep this record does not reproduce, which is stated wherever a figure computed from it appears.

(3) If the published receipt chain names a transaction hash for every transaction the wallet sent over the window - if the count of distinct hashes the chain asserts reaches the amount the wallet's transaction count advanced by - the attribution limb is refuted, and this result may then be described as the agent's rather than the wallet's. Reaching it would not by itself establish that the agent's engine signed them; it would remove the count that establishes it did not sign most of them.

(4) If the receipt chain's enumerated key paths contain any leaf naming the native coin or a fee paid in it, the gas limb is refuted: the fees were inside the equity series after all, the exclusion is dropped and they are subtracted. The chain's data-purchase cost is a cost in USDC and not a fee in the native coin, so it does not refute this limb; it is published beside the headline with the result that would follow if all of it had left this wallet, because that reading and the owner's sweep disagree.

Whichever way each limb comes out is published. The claim is written as the unflattering statement, so a falsifier that does not fire leaves a loss standing, and surviving it is not a result in the agent's favour and is not to be read as one. Nothing here can refute 06: 06's funding limb is about the fields inside its own corpus and this evidence is outside that corpus, so 06's claim and falsifier are unchanged and this record is an addition beside them.

metric.formula:
Everything is read from the two registered corpora and nothing is fetched while it is computed. The dataset is the frozen on-chain corpus; the receipt chain 06 registered is read alongside it at docket/advantage/v2/corpus/trading/solvent-receipts.json for the three things only it can supply - the window's own endpoint seconds, the set of transaction hashes the agent published, and the enumerated key paths the gas limb is searched over.

THE UNIT OF ACCOUNT. USDT and USDC on BSC are valued at one dollar each and no other token is valued at all. That is not a convenience: SOLVENT's own engine marks stables at min(price, 1.0) and never above, both window boundaries are held in those two alone, and both deposits are one of them - so every term in the headline is exact without a price source. Every balance is read as an integer of the token's own atomic units, scaled by decimals() read from the token contract rather than assumed, and carried in decimal arithmetic; no float touches a balance.

THE WINDOW, AS BLOCKS. The opening block is 104992551 and the closing block is 106969455, and neither is chosen: each carries the whole second one of the receipt chain's own endpoint receipts records, and that identity is asserted rather than assumed. BSC produces more than one block a second in this range, so the corpus carries the block either side of each and the report asserts the dollar-pegged balance is identical across all three, which is what makes the two headline readings independent of which block is picked.

WHAT COUNTS AS AN EXTERNAL DEPOSIT, fixed here and not once the transactions are visible. A transfer of value into the wallet whose transaction some other address sent: tx.from != the wallet. Both legs of every trade the account made are transactions the wallet itself sent, so no swap can enter this set however much value it moved, and the rule turns on who sent the transaction rather than on a judgement about which of the wallet's own transactions looked like funding. Twelve properties are recomputed per deposit from the frozen transaction and receipt rather than read off the corpus, and they are reported one by one rather than as a verdict: it succeeded; it sent no native value; it called the BSC-USD contract; its calldata is the transfer selector and exactly two arguments; it emitted exactly one log; that log carries the canonical Transfer topic and the token's own address; it credited this wallet; it came from the transaction's own sender; that sender is not the wallet; that sender returns 0x from eth_getCode; the amount the log carries equals the wallet's BSC-USD balance delta across the block containing it; and the transaction's block agrees with its receipt's. The Transfer topic and the transfer selector are derived by keccak from their signatures rather than transcribed.

THE HEADLINE. deposit_adjusted_pnl_usd = closing dollar-pegged balance - opening dollar-pegged balance - external deposits, reported beside each of those three terms and beside the balance change the first two make. It needs no price mark and it is the figure the claim is about.

THE TWO PERCENTAGES, both from that one numerator, because a reader asking how the money did and a reader asking how much of the contributions came back are asking different questions and each is entitled to the count that answers theirs. Modified Dietz divides it by the opening balance plus each deposit weighted by the fraction of the window still to run when it arrived, the weights taken in the block timestamps' own seconds, and the convention is published with the figure because a calendar-day convention would move it slightly and a reader must not have to guess which was used. The second divides it by the opening balance plus every dollar ever paid in. Both are reported as {numerator, denominator, value} and neither is reported without the other.

THE TIME-WEIGHTED RETURN IS NOT PUBLISHED AS A FIGURE, and that is registered here rather than decided once the spread was visible. Chain-linking needs the account valued at every flow, and at the second deposit most of the account's value sits in ETH, which no balanceOf can price and for which this record observed no price source. So it is computed as a function of that mark over the registered grid 1400, 1500, 1600, 1700, 1800 US dollars and published as a table: every sub-period's opening and closing value, its return, the linked product, and the lowest and highest the grid produces. The grid's span is the sensitivity and it is published as such. No row is the answer and none is offered as one.

ATTRIBUTION. The wallet's transaction count is read at the opening and closing block and their difference is the number of transactions the key sent. The set of distinct transaction hashes the receipt chain asserts - over execution_seal.tx_hash and executions[].tx_hash - is counted from the registered chain. The difference is reported as {numerator, denominator, value} over the transactions sent and is stated as a floor rather than an exact count, because a hash the chain asserts need not be one the wallet sent and 06 records that 10 of them name a transaction the chain never confirms. The owner's log sweep - 44 value-moving transactions found, 16 absent from the chain's executions, including the two largest - is carried with its method and marked as not reproduced by this module. The two named prefixes are checked against the chain's own hash set here and the result of that check is published.

GAS. The receipt chain's enumerated key paths are searched for a leaf naming the native coin or a fee paid in it, and the matches are published. Gas is excluded from every figure and the exclusion runs one way: every fee made the account smaller, so the loss is a floor. The count of transactions sent and the count of their hashes this record holds are both published, because their gap is why the fee total cannot be computed. Separately the chain's own recorded data-purchase cost is totalled and the result that would follow if all of it had left this wallet is published beside the headline, because that reading and the owner's sweep disagree and this record states the disagreement rather than settling it.

NOTHING IS FETCHED, SIGNED OR SENT. The corpus is a set of raw JSON-RPC answers taken once at the recorded fetched_at, digested, and read from disk thereafter. No transaction of any kind was made at any point in producing this record.
metric.name: deposit_adjusted_pnl_usd
metric.units: US dollars over one closed window

null_baselines.name: count_the_balance_change_as_the_result
null_baselines.what_it_does: Reads the account's closing dollar-pegged balance minus its opening one as the result, taking no view on where the money came from. Computed by docket.advantage.v2.deposits.count_the_balance_change over the same two readings the registered arm uses, and reported in US dollars - never as a ratio, because the ratio of those two readings is the naive figure this whole record exists to refuse.
null_baselines.why_it_is_the_right_null: It is the reading a reader gets for free. Two balances published either side of a window invite subtraction, and subtraction is the arithmetic anyone does first. It requires knowing nothing about the account's transfers, which is exactly what makes it the ceiling the registered arm has to be measured under, and the distance between the two is precisely the money that was paid in. If they were equal, nothing external had reached the account and the balance change would be the result.

null_baselines.name: hold_the_stables
null_baselines.what_it_does: Gives a portfolio the same opening balance and the same two contributions at the same moments, holds them in the dollar-pegged tokens they arrived in, and sends no transaction. Its closing balance is what was put into it and its deposit-adjusted result is therefore zero. Computed by docket.advantage.v2.deposits.hold_the_stables from the same readings.
null_baselines.why_it_is_the_right_null: It is the arm an execution record has to be measured against, because the question a trading record answers is whether trading beat leaving the money alone. Every boundary and both flows here are dollar-pegged, so this arm needs no assumption and no price: it is exact. It also sends no transaction, so it pays no gas, which is the second direction the comparison runs in and the one that makes the registered arm's excluded fees a real cost rather than a rounding note. The whole of the registered arm's distance from zero is the cost of having traded at all.

question: What did SOLVENT's account return over the same closed window the 06 record covers, once the money paid into it from outside is subtracted - and how much of that figure can be attributed to the agent rather than to the key that signed for it?
stopping_rule:
Ten pinned blocks, each read once: the window's opening and closing block, the block containing each of the two deposits and the block before each of them, and the block either side of the two window blocks. Nothing is re-read because its answer was unwelcome and nothing is dropped after its answer is visible - the window closed on 2026-06-29 and every one of these blocks is final.

The ordering this registration can and cannot claim is worth stating plainly, because it is weaker than the word pre-registration usually carries, and it is weaker in the same way 06's is. A chain cannot be hashed before it is read, so the corpus was frozen first and this registration was written against its digest. More than that: the deposit amounts, the two balance totals and the deposit-adjusted result were all known before this specification was written - they are in the brief this work was done to - and the mark grid was chosen knowing which token the second boundary held. So this registration was not written in ignorance of its own headline and does not pretend to have been. What it fixes before the arithmetic is the part that decides what the figures mean: what counts as an external deposit and why a trade leg cannot be one, which tokens are valued and at what, which denominators are published and why both, that the time-weighted return is a table and not a figure, that gas is excluded and in which direction, that the deposit set is owner-attested rather than swept here, and the sentence that would refute each limb.
